annotationRationale: Complementing two digits gives a bijection with nonnegative four-part sums of 9. Stars and bars counts those sums using a combination.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official solution, explicitly checking the upper bounds and inverse correspondence and explaining the separator count.

review.mathCheck: The invertible substitution \((a,b,c,d)\mapsto(9-a,b,9-c,d)\) converts the condition into four nonnegative integers summing to 9. Their upper bounds are automatic. Thus there are \(\binom{12}{3}=220\) polynomials, choice D, with leading zero coefficients correctly included.
review.sourceMethodCheck: An originally worded, faithful adaptation of the first MAA Q22 approach on page 14. It retains complementing digits and stars and bars, while explicitly supplying the inverse correspondence and explaining empty groups.
review.annotationCheck: Digit bounds, lower degrees, uniqueness and completeness are justified. The separator explanation is sufficient for an AMC 12 student.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact links for cnm_h237 and cnm_029 fit combination evaluation and substitution at -1 as background. Neither supplies national coverage of the assessed bijection and stars-and-bars skills.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 6.EE.A.2c and the evaluation portion of 6.EE.A.2 support substitution with powers. This demonstrates only their evaluation aspect, not full expression-writing scope or the combinatorial method.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: math:stars-and-bars and math:bijective-counting are directly assessed. cnm_h237 and cnm_029 correctly support the binomial calculation and evaluation of P(-1).
